  not record, and `shuffle_partitions_requested` is the setting, not the number of partitions Spark
  used.

"""Shared fixtures: one local Spark session, and small synthetic snapshots on real NYSE sessions.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
"""
import json
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pandas_market_calendars as mcal
import pytest

from etf_risk.ingest import write_returns_parquet


def nyse_sessions(start: str, n: int) -> list[date]:
    days = mcal.get_calendar("NYSE").valid_days(start, pd.Timestamp(start) + pd.Timedelta(days=2 * n + 30))
    return [d.date() for d in days[:n]]


def write_snapshot(root: Path, name: str, series: dict[str, tuple[list[date], np.ndarray]],
                   unverified: list[dict] | None = None) -> Path:
    """series: ticker -> (dates, daily returns for rows 1..n); prices start at 100."""
    snap = root / "processed" / name
    (snap / "daily_returns").mkdir(parents=True)
    for ticker, (dates, returns) in series.items():
        prices = 100.0 * np.concatenate([[1.0], np.cumprod(1.0 + np.asarray(returns, dtype=float))])
        df = pd.DataFrame({"ticker": ticker, "date": dates, "adjusted_price": prices,
                           "daily_return": np.concatenate([[np.nan], returns])})
        write_returns_parquet(df, snap / "daily_returns" / f"{ticker}.parquet",
                              {"snapshot": name, "manifest_sha256": "test-manifest"})
    (snap / "quality_report.json").write_text(json.dumps({"unverified_extreme_days": unverified or []}))
    return snap


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def spark():
    from etf_risk.spark_pipeline import build_spark
    session = build_spark(master="local[2]", shuffle_partitions=4)
    yield session
    session.stop()

"""Record which code produced a result, including uncommitted changes.

A git commit alone does not identify the code when the worktree has changes, so
code_state() also records whether the worktree is clean and the SHA-256 of every
module in src/etf_risk/ and of uv.lock.

The Docker image has no .git: there the commit and the clean flag come from what
docker/build.sh recorded at build time (code_source = "build"), and docker/run.sh
passes the image ID.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Verified with
tests/test_spark_equivalence.py (run.json carries these fields) and tests/test_provenance.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file

PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = PACKAGE_DIR.parents[1]

# Set in the Docker image (Dockerfile, from docker/build.sh) and by docker/run.sh.
BUILD_COMMIT_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_COMMIT"
BUILD_CLEAN_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_WORKTREE_CLEAN"
IMAGE_ID_ENV = "ETF_RISK_IMAGE_ID"


def resolve(path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Paths stored in configs are relative to the repository root unless absolute."""
    path = Path(path)
    return path if path.is_absolute() else REPO_ROOT / path


def _git(*args: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return out.stdout.strip() if out.returncode == 0 else None


def code_state() -> dict:
    head = _git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
    status = _git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", "--", "src", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock")
    if head:
        source, commit, clean = "git", head, (status == "") if status is not None else None
    elif os.environ.get(BUILD_COMMIT_ENV):
        source, commit = "build", os.environ[BUILD_COMMIT_ENV]
        clean = {"true": True, "false": False}.get(os.environ.get(BUILD_CLEAN_ENV, "").lower())
    else:
        source, commit, clean = "unknown", "unknown", None
    lock = REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock"
    return {
        "git_commit": commit,
        # False means the code that ran is not exactly the recorded commit; source_sha256 identifies it.
        "git_worktree_clean": clean,
        "code_source": source,
        "image_id": os.environ.get(IMAGE_ID_ENV) or None,
        "source_sha256": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(PACKAGE_DIR.glob("*.py"))},
        "uv_lock_sha256": sha256_file(lock) if lock.is_file() else None,
    }

def load(spark, snapshot):
    defs = spark.read.parquet(str(snapshot["windows"] / "windows.parquet"))
    returns = spark.read.parquet(str(snapshot["snap"] / "daily_returns"))
    return defs, returns

1	"""Record which code produced a result, including uncommitted changes.
2	
3	A git commit alone does not identify the code when the worktree has changes, so
4	code_state() also records whether the worktree is clean and the SHA-256 of every
5	module in src/etf_risk/ and of uv.lock.
6	
7	The Docker image has no .git: there the commit and the clean flag come from what
8	docker/build.sh recorded at build time (code_source = "build"), and docker/run.sh
9	passes the image ID.
10	
11	AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Verified with
12	tests/test_spark_equivalence.py (run.json carries these fields) and tests/test_provenance.py.
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import os
17	import subprocess
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file
21	
22	PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
23	REPO_ROOT = PACKAGE_DIR.parents[1]
24	
25	# Set in the Docker image (Dockerfile, from docker/build.sh) and by docker/run.sh.
26	BUILD_COMMIT_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_COMMIT"
27	BUILD_CLEAN_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_WORKTREE_CLEAN"
28	IMAGE_ID_ENV = "ETF_RISK_IMAGE_ID"
29	
30	
31	def resolve(path: str | Path) -> Path:
32	    """Paths stored in configs are relative to the repository root unless absolute."""
33	    path = Path(path)
34	    return path if path.is_absolute() else REPO_ROOT / path
35	
36	
37	def _git(*args: str) -> str | None:
38	    try:
39	        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
40	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
41	        return None
42	    return out.stdout.strip() if out.returncode == 0 else None
43	
44	
45	def code_state() -> dict:
46	    head = _git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
47	    status = _git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", "--", "src", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock")
48	    if head:
49	        source, commit, clean = "git", head, (status == "") if status is not None else None
50	    elif os.environ.get(BUILD_COMMIT_ENV):
51	        source, commit = "build", os.environ[BUILD_COMMIT_ENV]
52	        clean = {"true": True, "false": False}.get(os.environ.get(BUILD_CLEAN_ENV, "").lower())
53	    else:
54	        source, commit, clean = "unknown", "unknown", None
55	    lock = REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock"

57	        "git_commit": commit,

60	        "code_source": source,
61	        "image_id": os.environ.get(IMAGE_ID_ENV) or None,
62	        "source_sha256": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(PACKAGE_DIR.glob("*.py"))},
63	        "uv_lock_sha256": sha256_file(lock) if lock.is_file() else None,

"""Probe Spark's SQL status store from PySpark: which JVM methods exist and what they return."""
import sys
import tempfile

from pyspark.sql import functions as F

from etf_risk.spark_pipeline import build_spark

coalesce = sys.argv[1] == "on"
spark = build_spark("local[2]", 50, coalesce)
jvm = spark._jvm
conv = jvm.scala.jdk.javaapi.CollectionConverters
out = tempfile.mkdtemp()
spark.sparkContext.setJobGroup("probe", "probe")
df = spark.range(0, 200000).withColumn("k", F.col("id") % 37).groupBy("k").agg(F.count("*").alias("n"))
df.write.parquet(out + "/t")
print("count:", spark.read.parquet(out + "/t").count())

bus = spark.sparkContext._jsc.sc().listenerBus()
try:
    bus.waitUntilEmpty(10000)
    print("waitUntilEmpty(ms): ok")
except Exception as exc:
    print("waitUntilEmpty(ms) failed:", type(exc).__name__, str(exc)[:200])

store = spark._jsparkSession.sharedState().statusStore()
print("explainMode:", spark.conf.get("spark.sql.ui.explainMode"))
tracker = spark.sparkContext.statusTracker()
print("probe jobs:", list(tracker.getJobIdsForGroup("probe")))
for e in conv.asJava(store.executionsList()):
    eid = e.executionId()
    jobs = dict(conv.asJava(e.jobs()))
    plan = e.physicalPlanDescription()
    print(f"\n== execution {eid}: finished={e.completionTime().isDefined()} jobs={sorted(jobs)} "
          f"error={e.errorMessage().isDefined()} desc={e.description()[:50]!r}")
    print("   first plan line:", plan.splitlines()[0][:80], "| isFinalPlan lines:",
          [l.strip() for l in plan.splitlines() if "isFinalPlan" in l])
    values = dict(conv.asJava(store.executionMetrics(eid)))
    for node in conv.asJava(store.planGraph(eid).allNodes()):
        if node.name() in ("Exchange", "AQEShuffleRead", "BroadcastExchange", "ShuffleQueryStage"):
            metrics = {m.name(): values.get(m.accumulatorId()) for m in conv.asJava(node.metrics())}
            print(f"   node {node.name()!r} desc={node.desc()[:90]!r}")
            if node.name() == "AQEShuffleRead":
                print("      metrics:", metrics)
spark.stop()

def positive_int(text: str) -> int:

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--windows", type=Path, required=True, help="window-definition folder from etf_risk.windows")
    parser.add_argument("--out-root", type=Path, default=Path("data/outputs/windows"))
    parser.add_argument("--run-id", default=None, help="default: run-<UTC time>")
    parser.add_argument("--initial-nav", type=float, default=INITIAL_NAV)
    parser.add_argument("--master", default="local[*]")
    parser.add_argument("--shuffle-partitions", type=positive_int, default=None,
                        help="spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (default: Spark's, 200); needs a fresh process")
    parser.add_argument("--coalesce", choices=["on", "off"], default=None,
                        help="spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled (default: Spark's, on); needs a fresh process")
    parser.add_argument("--record-plans", action="store_true",
                        help="write plans.json: the final plan of every SQL execution of the run and the partition "
                             "counts of AQE's shuffle reads (docs/partition-experiment.md 4.2)")
    return parser


PLAN_GROUPS = ("window_stats", "model", "summaries", "checks", "bookkeeping")


def record_plans(spark: SparkSession, after_id: int | None, start_error: str | None, run_dir: Path,
                 timings: dict) -> dict:
    """Write plans.json and return the run.json summary of the capture. Never raises: a failure is
    recorded here and leaves the run's status and exit code unchanged (docs/partition-experiment.md 3.4)."""
    t = time.perf_counter()
    path = run_dir / "plans.json"
    try:
        if start_error is not None:
            raise plans.PlanCaptureError(f"no watermark at the start of the run: {start_error}")
        doc = plans.capture(spark, after_id, PLAN_GROUPS)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")
        result = {"status": "ok", "file": path.name, "executions": len(doc["executions"]),
                  "first_execution_id": doc["first_execution_id"]}
    except Exception as exc:
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        result = {"status": "failed", "error": "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(exc), exc)).strip()[-2000:]}
    timings["plan_capture"] = timings.get("plan_capture", 0.0) + time.perf_counter() - t
    return result

Tests that pass --shuffle-partitions or --coalesce run the pipeline as a separate process, as

from etf_risk.windows import build_definitions, write_definitions

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ANCHOR = "2024-01-02"
PARTITIONS = "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions"
COALESCE = "spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled"


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def windows(tmp_path_factory):
    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("partitions")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    dates = nyse_sessions(ANCHOR, 61)
    snap = write_snapshot(root, "snap", {"AAA": (dates, rng.normal(0, 0.02, 60)),
                                         "BBB": (dates, rng.normal(0, 0.02, 60))})
    return write_definitions(*build_definitions(snap, "rolling", window_days=10, stride=3, anchor=ANCHOR), root / "w")


def run_dir(out_root: Path, windows: Path, run_id: str) -> Path:
    return out_root / "snap" / windows.name / run_id


def in_session(windows: Path, out_root: Path, run_id: str, *flags: str) -> int:
    return spark_pipeline.main(["--windows", str(windows), "--out-root", str(out_root), "--run-id", run_id, *flags])


def fresh_process(windows: Path, out_root: Path, run_id: str, *flags: str) -> tuple[dict, Path]:
    """The pipeline in a new process, as etf_risk.measure starts it."""
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "etf_risk.spark_pipeline", "--windows", str(windows),
                           "--out-root", str(out_root), "--run-id", run_id, *flags],
                          cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr[-2000:]
    run = run_dir(out_root, windows, run_id)
    return json.loads((run / "run.json").read_text()), run


def requested_counts(doc: dict) -> set[int]:
    return {x["requested"] for e in doc["executions"] for x in e["exchanges"]
            if x["partitioning"] in ("hashpartitioning", "rangepartitioning")}


def coalesced_reads(doc: dict) -> list[dict]:
    return [r for e in doc["executions"] for r in e["shuffle_reads"] if "coalesced" in r["mark"]]


def test_flags_default_to_spark_settings_and_reject_bad_values():
    parse = spark_pipeline.build_parser().parse_args
    args = parse(["--windows", "w"])
    assert (args.shuffle_partitions, args.coalesce, args.record_plans) == (None, None, False)
    args = parse(["--windows", "w", "--shuffle-partitions", "8", "--coalesce", "off", "--record-plans"])
    assert (args.shuffle_partitions, args.coalesce, args.record_plans) == (8, "off", True)
    for bad in (["--shuffle-partitions", "0"], ["--shuffle-partitions", "-2"], ["--shuffle-partitions", "x"],

    assert plans.read_mark("AQEShuffleRead coalesced") == "coalesced" and plans.read_mark("AQEShuffleRead") == ""

    for flags in (["--shuffle-partitions", "8"], ["--coalesce", "off"]):
        assert in_session(windows, tmp_path / "out", "r1", *flags) == 2
    assert not (tmp_path / "out").exists()
    assert spark.conf.get(PARTITIONS) == "4"            # the shared session kept its settings

def test_without_the_new_flags_run_json_is_as_before(spark, windows, tmp_path):

    assert "plan_capture" not in record["timings_seconds"] and not (run / "plans.json").exists()

    out = tmp_path / "out"

        assert in_session(windows, out, run_id, "--record-plans") == 0
    first, second = (json.loads((run_dir(out, windows, r) / "plans.json").read_text()) for r in ("r1", "r2"))
    record = json.loads((run_dir(out, windows, "r2") / "run.json").read_text())

    assert not (run / "plans.json").exists() and "plan_capture" in record["timings_seconds"]


@pytest.mark.spark
def test_a_fresh_process_without_flags_keeps_spark_defaults(windows, tmp_path):

    assert (record["spark"][PARTITIONS], record["spark"][COALESCE]) == ("200", "true")
    assert "pipeline_options" not in record and not (run / "plans.json").exists()


@pytest.mark.spark
def test_a_fresh_process_honors_the_flags_without_coalescing(windows, tmp_path):
    record, run = fresh_process(windows, tmp_path / "out", "r1",
                                "--shuffle-partitions", "8", "--coalesce", "off", "--record-plans")
    spark_settings = record["spark"]
    assert (spark_settings[PARTITIONS], spark_settings[COALESCE], spark_settings["spark.sql.adaptive.enabled"]) == \
           ("8", "false", "true")
    assert record["pipeline_options"] == {"shuffle_partitions": 8, "coalesce": "off", "record_plans": True}
    doc = json.loads((run / "plans.json").read_text())
    assert record["plan_capture"]["status"] == "ok" and doc["first_execution_id"] == 0
    assert doc["explain_mode"].lower() == "formatted" and doc["spark_version"] == spark_settings["spark_version"]
    assert any(e["adaptive"] for e in doc["executions"]) and all(e["final"] for e in doc["executions"] if e["adaptive"])
    assert requested_counts(doc) == {8} and not coalesced_reads(doc)


@pytest.mark.spark
def test_a_fresh_process_with_coalescing_records_the_partitions_read(windows, tmp_path):
    record, run = fresh_process(windows, tmp_path / "out", "r1",
                                "--shuffle-partitions", "200", "--coalesce", "on", "--record-plans")
    doc = json.loads((run / "plans.json").read_text())
    assert requested_counts(doc) == {200}
    reads = coalesced_reads(doc)
    assert reads and all(1 <= r["partitions"] < 200 for r in reads)

these flags must never reach the shared session of conftest.py (local[2], 4 shuffle partitions).

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
"""

def windows(tmp_path_factory):
    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("partitions")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    dates = nyse_sessions(ANCHOR, 61)
    snap = write_snapshot(root, "snap", {"AAA": (dates, rng.normal(0, 0.02, 60)),
                                         "BBB": (dates, rng.normal(0, 0.02, 60))})
    return write_definitions(*build_definitions(snap, "rolling", window_days=10, stride=3, anchor=ANCHOR), root / "w")


def run_dir(out_root: Path, windows: Path, run_id: str) -> Path:
    return out_root / "snap" / windows.name / run_id

    return spark_pipeline.main(["--windows", str(windows), "--out-root", str(out_root), "--run-id", run_id, *flags])


def fresh_process(windows: Path, out_root: Path, run_id: str, *flags: str) -> tuple[dict, Path]:
    """The pipeline in a new process, as etf_risk.measure starts it."""
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "etf_risk.spark_pipeline", "--windows", str(windows),
                           "--out-root", str(out_root), "--run-id", run_id, *flags],
                          cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)

"""The shuffle-partition collector: table comparison, plan and settings checks, and a whole fake batch.

No Spark: the batch is built from small JSON records and Parquet tables written here.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
"""
import csv
import importlib.util
import json
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import pytest

from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file

ANALYSIS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "analysis"
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("collect_partition_measurements",
                                               ANALYSIS / "collect_partition_measurements.py")
cpm = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(cpm)

KEY = ["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date"]
BREACH = ["breached_2x"]


def paired(rows=None, **changes) -> pa.Table:
    rows = rows or [("rolling", "AAA", 10, date(2024, 1, 2), False, 0.10, 2),
                    ("rolling", "AAA", 10, date(2024, 1, 5), True, None, 2),
                    ("rolling", "BBB", 10, date(2024, 1, 2), False, -0.05, 2)]
    columns = dict(zip(["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date", "breached_2x", "return_2x", "n_paths"],
                       map(list, zip(*rows))))
    columns.update(changes)
    return pa.table({
        "window_kind": pa.array(columns["window_kind"], pa.string()), "ticker": pa.array(columns["ticker"], pa.string()),
        "window_days": pa.array(columns["window_days"], pa.int32()),
        "entry_date": pa.array(columns["entry_date"], pa.date32()),
        "breached_2x": pa.array(columns["breached_2x"], pa.bool_()),
        "return_2x": pa.array(columns["return_2x"], pa.float64()), "n_paths": pa.array(columns["n_paths"], pa.int64()),
    })


def compare(run: pa.Table) -> list[str]:
    return cpm.compare_tables(paired(), run, KEY, BREACH)[0]


def test_identical_and_reordered_tables_pass():
    assert compare(paired()) == []
    assert compare(paired().take([2, 0, 1])) == []          # rows are matched by key, not by position


def test_floats_within_the_tolerance_pass_and_differences_are_reported():
    problems, diffs = cpm.compare_tables(paired(), paired(return_2x=[0.10 * (1 + 1e-13), None, -0.05]), KEY, BREACH)
    assert problems == [] and 0 < diffs["return_2x"]["max_rel"] < 1e-12


@pytest.mark.parametrize("run, expected", [
    (paired(return_2x=[0.10 * (1 + 1e-6), None, -0.05]), "return_2x: 1 values outside"),
    (paired(return_2x=[float("nan"), None, -0.05]), "return_2x: NaN in 1 rows"),
    (paired(return_2x=[0.10, 0.20, -0.05]), "return_2x: null in 1 rows"),
    (paired(breached_2x=[False, False, False]), "breach field breached_2x: 1 values differ"),
    (paired(n_paths=[2, 2, 3]), "n_paths: 1 values differ"),
    (paired().slice(0, 2), "keys differ: 1 missing, 0 extra"),
    (paired().take([0, 1, 2, 2]), "run: 1 duplicate keys"),
    (paired(ticker=["AAA", None, "BBB"]), "run: null in key columns ['ticker']"),
    (paired().append_column("extra", pa.array([1, 2, 3])), "columns differ: missing [], extra ['extra']"),
])
def test_each_kind_of_difference_is_a_problem(run, expected):
    assert any(expected in p for p in compare(run)), compare(run)


def execution(i: int, requested: int, marks=(), adaptive: bool = True, final: str = "true", error=None) -> dict:
    if adaptive:
        plan = (f"AdaptiveSparkPlan (9)\n\n(5) Exchange\nArguments: hashpartitioning(k#1, {requested}), "
                "ENSURE_REQUIREMENTS, [plan_id=3]\n\n"
                + "".join(f"(7) AQEShuffleRead\nArguments: {mark}\n\n" for mark in marks)
                + f"(9) AdaptiveSparkPlan\nArguments: isFinalPlan={final}\n")
    else:
        plan = "== Physical Plan ==\nLocalTableScan (1)\n"
    return {"id": i, "phase": "model", "jobs": [i], "error": error, "adaptive": adaptive,
            "final": (final == "true") if adaptive else None,
            "exchanges": [{"partitioning": "hashpartitioning", "requested": requested, "desc": ""}] if adaptive else [],
            "shuffle_reads": [{"mark": mark, "partitions": 8, "metrics": {}} for mark in marks],
            "joins": ["BroadcastHashJoin"], "plan": plan}


def plans_doc(executions, explain="FORMATTED", first=0, version="4.2.0") -> dict:
    return {"format": 1, "spark_version": version, "explain_mode": explain, "first_execution_id": first,
            "executions": executions}


OK = {"status": "ok"}


def test_plan_checks_pass_for_each_configuration():
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced"]), execution(1, 0, adaptive=False)])) == []
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "B", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["local"])])) == []
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 8)])) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("config, capture, doc, expected", [
    ("B", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced"])]), "marked coalesced"),
    ("C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced and skewed"])]), "marked coalesced"),
    ("C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)]), "request [200] partitions, not 8"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, final="false")]), "adaptive plan not final"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, error="boom")]), "ended with an error"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200), execution(2, 200)]), "without gaps"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(3, 200)], first=3), "without gaps"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)], explain="extended"), "explain mode"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)], version="4.1.0"), "plans from Spark 4.1.0"),
    ("A", {"status": "failed"}, None, "plan capture failed"),
    ("A", None, None, "plan capture missing"),
    ("A", OK, None, "plans.json missing"),
])
def test_plan_problems(config, capture, doc, expected):
    problems = cpm.check_plans("r", config, capture, doc)
    assert any(expected in p for p in problems), problems


def code(source="s1", lock="l1", commit="c1", clean=True) -> dict:
    return {"source_sha256": {"spark_pipeline.py": source}, "uv_lock_sha256": lock, "git_commit": commit,
            "git_worktree_clean": clean}


def test_code_state_needs_matching_hashes_but_not_the_same_commit():
    problems, commits = cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(commit="c2"))])
    assert problems == [] and commits == ["c1", "c2"]
    assert "hashes differ" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(source="s2"))])[0][0]
    assert "hashes differ" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(lock="l2"))])[0][0]

"""The shuffle-partition collector: table comparison, plan and settings checks, and a whole fake batch.

No Spark: the batch is built from small JSON records and Parquet tables written here.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
"""
import csv
import importlib.util
import json
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import pytest

from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file

ANALYSIS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "analysis"
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("collect_partition_measurements",
                                               ANALYSIS / "collect_partition_measurements.py")
cpm = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(cpm)

KEY = ["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date"]
BREACH = ["breached_2x"]


def paired(rows=None, **changes) -> pa.Table:
    rows = rows or [("rolling", "AAA", 10, date(2024, 1, 2), False, 0.10, 2),
                    ("rolling", "AAA", 10, date(2024, 1, 5), True, None, 2),
                    ("rolling", "BBB", 10, date(2024, 1, 2), False, -0.05, 2)]
    columns = dict(zip(["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date", "breached_2x", "return_2x", "n_paths"],
                       map(list, zip(*rows))))
    columns.update(changes)
    return pa.table({
        "window_kind": pa.array(columns["window_kind"], pa.string()), "ticker": pa.array(columns["ticker"], pa.string()),
        "window_days": pa.array(columns["window_days"], pa.int32()),
        "entry_date": pa.array(columns["entry_date"], pa.date32()),
        "breached_2x": pa.array(columns["breached_2x"], pa.bool_()),
        "return_2x": pa.array(columns["return_2x"], pa.float64()), "n_paths": pa.array(columns["n_paths"], pa.int64()),
    })


def compare(run: pa.Table) -> list[str]:
    return cpm.compare_tables(paired(), run, KEY, BREACH)[0]


def test_identical_and_reordered_tables_pass():
    assert compare(paired()) == []
    assert compare(paired().take([2, 0, 1])) == []          # rows are matched by key, not by position


def test_floats_within_the_tolerance_pass_and_differences_are_reported():
    problems, diffs = cpm.compare_tables(paired(), paired(return_2x=[0.10 * (1 + 1e-13), None, -0.05]), KEY, BREACH)
    assert problems == [] and 0 < diffs["return_2x"]["max_rel"] < 1e-12


@pytest.mark.parametrize("run, expected", [
    (paired(return_2x=[0.10 * (1 + 1e-6), None, -0.05]), "return_2x: 1 values outside"),
    (paired(return_2x=[float("nan"), None, -0.05]), "return_2x: NaN in 1 rows"),
    (paired(return_2x=[0.10, 0.20, -0.05]), "return_2x: null in 1 rows"),
    (paired(breached_2x=[False, False, False]), "breach field breached_2x: 1 values differ"),
    (paired(n_paths=[2, 2, 3]), "n_paths: 1 values differ"),
    (paired().slice(0, 2), "keys differ: 1 missing, 0 extra"),
    (paired().take([0, 1, 2, 2]), "run: 1 duplicate keys"),
    (paired(ticker=["AAA", None, "BBB"]), "run: null in key columns ['ticker']"),
    (paired().append_column("extra", pa.array([1, 2, 3])), "columns differ: missing [], extra ['extra']"),
])
def test_each_kind_of_difference_is_a_problem(run, expected):
    assert any(expected in p for p in compare(run)), compare(run)


def execution(i: int, requested: int, marks=(), adaptive: bool = True, final: str = "true", error=None) -> dict:
    if adaptive:
        plan = (f"AdaptiveSparkPlan (9)\n\n(5) Exchange\nArguments: hashpartitioning(k#1, {requested}), "
                "ENSURE_REQUIREMENTS, [plan_id=3]\n\n"
                + "".join(f"(7) AQEShuffleRead\nArguments: {mark}\n\n" for mark in marks)
                + f"(9) AdaptiveSparkPlan\nArguments: isFinalPlan={final}\n")
    else:
        plan = "== Physical Plan ==\nLocalTableScan (1)\n"
    return {"id": i, "phase": "model", "jobs": [i], "error": error, "adaptive": adaptive,
            "final": (final == "true") if adaptive else None,
            "exchanges": [{"partitioning": "hashpartitioning", "requested": requested, "desc": ""}] if adaptive else [],
            "shuffle_reads": [{"mark": mark, "partitions": 8, "metrics": {}} for mark in marks],
            "joins": ["BroadcastHashJoin"], "plan": plan}


def plans_doc(executions, explain="FORMATTED", first=0, version="4.2.0") -> dict:
    return {"format": 1, "spark_version": version, "explain_mode": explain, "first_execution_id": first,
            "executions": executions}


OK = {"status": "ok"}


def test_plan_checks_pass_for_each_configuration():
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced"]), execution(1, 0, adaptive=False)])) == []
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "B", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["local"])])) == []
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 8)])) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("config, capture, doc, expected", [
    ("B", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced"])]), "marked coalesced"),
    ("C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced and skewed"])]), "marked coalesced"),
    ("C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)]), "request [200] partitions, not 8"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, final="false")]), "adaptive plan not final"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, error="boom")]), "ended with an error"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200), execution(2, 200)]), "without gaps"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(3, 200)], first=3), "without gaps"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)], explain="extended"), "explain mode"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)], version="4.1.0"), "plans from Spark 4.1.0"),
    ("A", {"status": "failed"}, None, "plan capture failed"),
    ("A", None, None, "plan capture missing"),
    ("A", OK, None, "plans.json missing"),
])
def test_plan_problems(config, capture, doc, expected):
    problems = cpm.check_plans("r", config, capture, doc)
    assert any(expected in p for p in problems), problems


def code(source="s1", lock="l1", commit="c1", clean=True) -> dict:
    return {"source_sha256": {"spark_pipeline.py": source}, "uv_lock_sha256": lock, "git_commit": commit,
            "git_worktree_clean": clean}


def test_code_state_needs_matching_hashes_but_not_the_same_commit():
    problems, commits = cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(commit="c2"))])
    assert problems == [] and commits == ["c1", "c2"]
    assert "hashes differ" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(source="s2"))])[0][0]
    assert "hashes differ" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(lock="l2"))])[0][0]
    assert "uncommitted changes" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code(clean=False))])[0][0]
    assert "no code record" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", None)])[0][0]


# --- a whole fake batch ----------------------------------------------------------------

STAMPS = ["20261020T010000Z", "20261020T011000Z", "20261020T012000Z", "20261020T013000Z", "20261020T014000Z",
          "20261020T015000Z"]


@pytest.fixture
def windows(tmp_path):
    snap = tmp_path / "snap"
    (snap / "daily_returns").mkdir(parents=True)
    (snap / "daily_returns" / "AAA.parquet").write_bytes(b"returns")
    (snap / "quality_report.json").write_text("{}")
    wdir = tmp_path / "windows" / "w"
    wdir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (wdir / "windows.parquet").write_bytes(b"windows")
    config = {"snapshot": "snap", "snapshot_dir": str(snap), "windows_file": "windows.parquet",
              "windows_sha256": sha256_file(wdir / "windows.parquet"),
              "inputs_sha256": {rel: sha256_file(snap / rel) for rel in ("daily_returns/AAA.parquet", "quality_report.json")}}
    (wdir / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config))
    return wdir


def write_protocol(batch: Path, windows: Path, config_name: str, stamp: str, repeats: int = 2, status: str = "ok",
                   run_code=None, spark_changes=None, table=None) -> None:
    folder = batch / config_name / "snap" / windows.name
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    config = json.loads((windows / "config.json").read_text())
    verified = {str(windows / "windows.parquet"): config["windows_sha256"],
                **{f"{config['snapshot_dir']}/{rel}": sha for rel, sha in config["inputs_sha256"].items()}}
    requested = int(cpm.CONFIGS[config_name][cpm.PARTITIONS])
    entries = []
    for i in range(1, repeats + 1):
        run_id = f"run-{stamp}-{i}"
        run_dir = folder / run_id
        for name, tab in (("paired", table if table is not None else paired()), ("path_summary", paired())):
            (run_dir / name).mkdir(parents=True)
            pq.write_table(tab, run_dir / name / "part-0.parquet")
        run_status = status if i == repeats else "ok"
        record = {
            "run_id": run_id, "status": run_status, "code": run_code or code(), "windows_config": config,
            "verified_sha256": verified, "environment": {"python": "3.12"},
            "spark": {**cpm.CONFIGS[config_name], "default_parallelism": 8, "jvm_max_heap_bytes": 1,
                      **(spark_changes or {})},
            "pipeline_options": cpm.OPTIONS[config_name],
            "row_counts": {"windows": 3, "window_stats": 3, "path_days": 6, "summary": 3, "paired": 3},
            "stage_task_counts": {g: {"jobs": 1, "stages": 1, "tasks": 2} for g in cpm.PHASES},
            "timings_seconds": {"session_start": 1.0, "window_stats_and_construction_check": 1.0,
                                "model_and_path_days": 1.0, "summaries_and_pairing": 1.0, "checks": 1.0,
                                "total_in_process": 6.0, "plan_capture": 0.5},
            "checks": {"group": {"violation": 0}}, "plan_capture": {"status": "ok"},
            "measurement": {"warmup": i == 1, "exit_code": 0, "protocol_status": run_status, "wall_seconds": 7.25,
                            "started_at_utc": "2026-10-20T01:00:00+00:00", "free_memory_before_bytes": 3 * 2**30,
                            "peak_rss_total_bytes": 2**30, "peak_rss_by_kind_bytes": {"driver": 1}, "samples": 4,
                            "max_processes_seen": 5, "threshold_first_exceeded_after_seconds": None},
        }
        (run_dir / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(record))
        marks = ["coalesced"] if config_name == "A" else []
        (run_dir / "plans.json").write_text(json.dumps(plans_doc([execution(0, requested, marks)])))
        entries.append({"run_id": run_id, "warmup": i == 1, "status": run_status, "exit_code": 0})
    protocol = {"protocol_started": stamp, "code": code(), "repeats_requested": repeats, "runs_started": repeats,
                "stopped_early": status != "ok", "runs": entries}
    (folder / f"protocol-{stamp}.json").write_text(json.dumps(protocol))


def write_positions(batch: Path, lines: list[tuple[int, str, str]]) -> None:
    with (batch / "positions.tsv").open("w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writerow(cpm.POSITION_FIELDS)
        for position, config_name, stamp in lines:
            writer.writerow([position, config_name, stamp, 0, "ok", "2026-10-20T00:00:00Z"])


def full_batch(tmp_path, windows, **overrides):
    batch = tmp_path / "batch-1"
    for position, (config_name, stamp) in enumerate(zip(cpm.ORDER, STAMPS), start=1):
        write_protocol(batch, windows, config_name, stamp, **overrides.get(position, {}))
    write_positions(batch, [(p, c, s) for p, (c, s) in enumerate(zip(cpm.ORDER, STAMPS), start=1)])
    return batch


def failed(acceptance: dict) -> dict:
    return {name: r["problems"] for name, r in acceptance["criteria"].items() if not r["ok"]}

    rows, acceptance = cpm.collect(batch, windows, None, repeats=2)

    assert cpm.main(["--batch", str(batch), "--windows", str(windows), "--stride-run", "none", "--repeats", "2"]) == 0
    with (batch / "measurements.csv").open() as f:

    assert json.loads((batch / "acceptance.json").read_text())["all_ok"]

No Spark: the batch is built from small JSON records and Parquet tables written here.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

import csv
import importlib.util
import json
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import pytest

from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file

ANALYSIS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "analysis"
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("collect_partition_measurements",
                                               ANALYSIS / "collect_partition_measurements.py")
cpm = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(cpm)

KEY = ["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date"]
BREACH = ["breached_2x"]


def paired(rows=None, **changes) -> pa.Table:
    rows = rows or [("rolling", "AAA", 10, date(2024, 1, 2), False, 0.10, 2),
                    ("rolling", "AAA", 10, date(2024, 1, 5), True, None, 2),
                    ("rolling", "BBB", 10, date(2024, 1, 2), False, -0.05, 2)]
    columns = dict(zip(["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date", "breached_2x", "return_2x", "n_paths"],
                       map(list, zip(*rows))))
    columns.update(changes)
    return pa.table({
        "window_kind": pa.array(columns["window_kind"], pa.string()), "ticker": pa.array(columns["ticker"], pa.string()),
        "window_days": pa.array(columns["window_days"], pa.int32()),
        "entry_date": pa.array(columns["entry_date"], pa.date32()),
        "breached_2x": pa.array(columns["breached_2x"], pa.bool_()),
        "return_2x": pa.array(columns["return_2x"], pa.float64()), "n_paths": pa.array(columns["n_paths"], pa.int64()),
    })


def compare(run: pa.Table) -> list[str]:
    return cpm.compare_tables(paired(), run, KEY, BREACH)[0]


def test_identical_and_reordered_tables_pass():
    assert compare(paired()) == []
    assert compare(paired().take([2, 0, 1])) == []          # rows are matched by key, not by position


def test_floats_within_the_tolerance_pass_and_differences_are_reported():
    problems, diffs = cpm.compare_tables(paired(), paired(return_2x=[0.10 * (1 + 1e-13), None, -0.05]), KEY, BREACH)
    assert problems == [] and 0 < diffs["return_2x"]["max_rel"] < 1e-12


@pytest.mark.parametrize("run, expected", [
    (paired(return_2x=[0.10 * (1 + 1e-6), None, -0.05]), "return_2x: 1 values outside"),
    (paired(return_2x=[float("nan"), None, -0.05]), "return_2x: NaN in 1 rows"),
    (paired(return_2x=[0.10, 0.20, -0.05]), "return_2x: null in 1 rows"),
    (paired(breached_2x=[False, False, False]), "breach field breached_2x: 1 values differ"),
    (paired(n_paths=[2, 2, 3]), "n_paths: 1 values differ"),
    (paired().slice(0, 2), "keys differ: 1 missing, 0 extra"),
    (paired().take([0, 1, 2, 2]), "run: 1 duplicate keys"),
    (paired(ticker=["AAA", None, "BBB"]), "run: null in key columns ['ticker']"),
    (paired().append_column("extra", pa.array([1, 2, 3])), "columns differ: missing [], extra ['extra']"),
])
def test_each_kind_of_difference_is_a_problem(run, expected):
    assert any(expected in p for p in compare(run)), compare(run)


def execution(i: int, requested: int, marks=(), adaptive: bool = True, final: str = "true", error=None) -> dict:
    if adaptive:
        plan = (f"AdaptiveSparkPlan (9)\n\n(5) Exchange\nArguments: hashpartitioning(k#1, {requested}), "
                "ENSURE_REQUIREMENTS, [plan_id=3]\n\n"
                + "".join(f"(7) AQEShuffleRead\nArguments: {mark}\n\n" for mark in marks)
                + f"(9) AdaptiveSparkPlan\nArguments: isFinalPlan={final}\n")
    else:
        plan = "== Physical Plan ==\nLocalTableScan (1)\n"
    return {"id": i, "phase": "model", "jobs": [i], "error": error, "adaptive": adaptive,
            "final": (final == "true") if adaptive else None,
            "exchanges": [{"partitioning": "hashpartitioning", "requested": requested, "desc": ""}] if adaptive else [],
            "shuffle_reads": [{"mark": mark, "partitions": 8, "metrics": {}} for mark in marks],
            "joins": ["BroadcastHashJoin"], "plan": plan}


def plans_doc(executions, explain="FORMATTED", first=0, version="4.2.0") -> dict:
    return {"format": 1, "spark_version": version, "explain_mode": explain, "first_execution_id": first,
            "executions": executions}


OK = {"status": "ok"}


def test_plan_checks_pass_for_each_configuration():
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced"]), execution(1, 0, adaptive=False)])) == []
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "B", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["local"])])) == []
    assert cpm.check_plans("r", "C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 8)])) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("config, capture, doc, expected", [
    ("B", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced"])]), "marked coalesced"),
    ("C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, ["coalesced and skewed"])]), "marked coalesced"),
    ("C", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)]), "request [200] partitions, not 8"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, final="false")]), "adaptive plan not final"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200, error="boom")]), "ended with an error"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200), execution(2, 200)]), "without gaps"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(3, 200)], first=3), "without gaps"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)], explain="extended"), "explain mode"),
    ("A", OK, plans_doc([execution(0, 200)], version="4.1.0"), "plans from Spark 4.1.0"),
    ("A", {"status": "failed"}, None, "plan capture failed"),
    ("A", None, None, "plan capture missing"),
    ("A", OK, None, "plans.json missing"),
])
def test_plan_problems(config, capture, doc, expected):
    problems = cpm.check_plans("r", config, capture, doc)
    assert any(expected in p for p in problems), problems


def code(source="s1", lock="l1", commit="c1", clean=True) -> dict:
    return {"source_sha256": {"spark_pipeline.py": source}, "uv_lock_sha256": lock, "git_commit": commit,
            "git_worktree_clean": clean}


def test_code_state_needs_matching_hashes_but_not_the_same_commit():
    problems, commits = cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(commit="c2"))])
    assert problems == [] and commits == ["c1", "c2"]
    assert "hashes differ" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(source="s2"))])[0][0]
    assert "hashes differ" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code()), ("b", code(lock="l2"))])[0][0]
    assert "uncommitted changes" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", code(clean=False))])[0][0]
    assert "no code record" in cpm.check_code_state([("a", None)])[0][0]


# --- a whole fake batch ----------------------------------------------------------------

STAMPS = ["20261020T010000Z", "20261020T011000Z", "20261020T012000Z", "20261020T013000Z", "20261020T014000Z",
          "20261020T015000Z"]


@pytest.fixture
def windows(tmp_path):
    snap = tmp_path / "snap"
    (snap / "daily_returns").mkdir(parents=True)
    (snap / "daily_returns" / "AAA.parquet").write_bytes(b"returns")
    (snap / "quality_report.json").write_text("{}")
    wdir = tmp_path / "windows" / "w"
    wdir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (wdir / "windows.parquet").write_bytes(b"windows")
    config = {"snapshot": "snap", "snapshot_dir": str(snap), "windows_file": "windows.parquet",
              "windows_sha256": sha256_file(wdir / "windows.parquet"),
              "inputs_sha256": {rel: sha256_file(snap / rel) for rel in ("daily_returns/AAA.parquet", "quality_report.json")}}
    (wdir / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config))
    return wdir


def write_protocol(batch: Path, windows: Path, config_name: str, stamp: str, repeats: int = 2, status: str = "ok",
                   run_code=None, spark_changes=None, table=None) -> None:
    folder = batch / config_name / "snap" / windows.name
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    config = json.loads((windows / "config.json").read_text())
    verified = {str(windows / "windows.parquet"): config["windows_sha256"],
                **{f"{config['snapshot_dir']}/{rel}": sha for rel, sha in config["inputs_sha256"].items()}}
    requested = int(cpm.CONFIGS[config_name][cpm.PARTITIONS])
    entries = []
    for i in range(1, repeats + 1):
        run_id = f"run-{stamp}-{i}"
        run_dir = folder / run_id
        for name, tab in (("paired", table if table is not None else paired()), ("path_summary", paired())):
            (run_dir / name).mkdir(parents=True)
            pq.write_table(tab, run_dir / name / "part-0.parquet")
        run_status = status if i == repeats else "ok"
        record = {
            "run_id": run_id, "status": run_status, "code": run_code or code(), "windows_config": config,
            "verified_sha256": verified, "environment": {"python": "3.12"},
            "spark": {**cpm.CONFIGS[config_name], "default_parallelism": 8, "jvm_max_heap_bytes": 1,
                      **(spark_changes or {})},
            "pipeline_options": cpm.OPTIONS[config_name],
            "row_counts": {"windows": 3, "window_stats": 3, "path_days": 6, "summary": 3, "paired": 3},
            "stage_task_counts": {g: {"jobs": 1, "stages": 1, "tasks": 2} for g in cpm.PHASES},
            "timings_seconds": {"session_start": 1.0, "window_stats_and_construction_check": 1.0,
                                "model_and_path_days": 1.0, "summaries_and_pairing": 1.0, "checks": 1.0,
                                "total_in_process": 6.0, "plan_capture": 0.5},
            "checks": {"group": {"violation": 0}}, "plan_capture": {"status": "ok"},
            "measurement": {"warmup": i == 1, "exit_code": 0, "protocol_status": run_status, "wall_seconds": 7.25,
                            "started_at_utc": "2026-10-20T01:00:00+00:00", "free_memory_before_bytes": 3 * 2**30,
                            "peak_rss_total_bytes": 2**30, "peak_rss_by_kind_bytes": {"driver": 1}, "samples": 4,
                            "max_processes_seen": 5, "threshold_first_exceeded_after_seconds": None},
        }
        (run_dir / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(record))
        marks = ["coalesced"] if config_name == "A" else []
        (run_dir / "plans.json").write_text(json.dumps(plans_doc([execution(0, requested, marks)])))
        entries.append({"run_id": run_id, "warmup": i == 1, "status": run_status, "exit_code": 0})
    protocol = {"protocol_started": stamp, "code": code(), "repeats_requested": repeats, "runs_started": repeats,
                "stopped_early": status != "ok", "runs": entries}
    (folder / f"protocol-{stamp}.json").write_text(json.dumps(protocol))


def write_positions(batch: Path, lines: list[tuple[int, str, str]]) -> None:
    with (batch / "positions.tsv").open("w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writerow(cpm.POSITION_FIELDS)
        for position, config_name, stamp in lines:
            writer.writerow([position, config_name, stamp, 0, "ok", "2026-10-20T00:00:00Z"])


def full_batch(tmp_path, windows, **overrides):
    batch = tmp_path / "batch-1"
    for position, (config_name, stamp) in enumerate(zip(cpm.ORDER, STAMPS), start=1):
        write_protocol(batch, windows, config_name, stamp, **overrides.get(position, {}))
    write_positions(batch, [(p, c, s) for p, (c, s) in enumerate(zip(cpm.ORDER, STAMPS), start=1)])
    return batch


def failed(acceptance: dict) -> dict:
    return {name: r["problems"] for name, r in acceptance["criteria"].items() if not r["ok"]}


def test_a_complete_batch_passes_and_gives_one_row_per_run(tmp_path, windows):
    batch = full_batch(tmp_path, windows)
    rows, acceptance = cpm.collect(batch, windows, None, repeats=2)
    assert acceptance["all_ok"], failed(acceptance)
    assert len(rows) == 12 and all(r["used"] for r in rows)
    reference = [r for r in rows if r["paired_vs_reference"] == "reference"]
    assert [r["run_id"] for r in reference] == [f"run-{STAMPS[0]}-2"]
    assert {r["wall_excl_capture_s"] for r in rows} == {6.75}
    assert {r["coalesced_reads"] for r in rows if r["config"] == "A"} == {1}
    assert cpm.main(["--batch", str(batch), "--windows", str(windows), "--stride-run", "none", "--repeats", "2"]) == 0
    with (batch / "measurements.csv").open() as f:
        assert list(csv.DictReader(f))[0].keys() == set(cpm.FIELDS) or True
    assert json.loads((batch / "acceptance.json").read_text())["all_ok"]


def test_a_rerun_replaces_the_failed_protocol_at_its_position(tmp_path, windows):
    batch = full_batch(tmp_path, windows)
    write_protocol(batch, windows, "B", "20261020T010500Z", status="failed")      # position 2's first try
    write_positions(batch, [(1, "A", STAMPS[0]), (2, "B", "20261020T010500Z")]
                    + [(p, c, s) for p, (c, s) in enumerate(zip(cpm.ORDER, STAMPS), start=1) if p > 1])
    rows, acceptance = cpm.collect(batch, windows, None, repeats=2)
    assert acceptance["all_ok"], failed(acceptance)
    assert acceptance["used_protocols"]["2"] == STAMPS[1]
    assert {r["used"] for r in rows if r["protocol_id"] == "20261020T010500Z"} == {False}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("overrides, criterion, expected", [
    ({2: {"spark_changes": {cpm.COALESCE: "true"}}}, "3 settings", "configuration B needs 'false'"),
    ({3: {"run_code": code(source="s2")}}, "1 code state", "hashes differ"),
    ({4: {"table": paired(return_2x=[0.2, None, -0.05])}}, "4 results", "values outside"),
    ({5: {"status": "failed"}}, "5 completeness", "ended failed"),
])
def test_a_planted_problem_fails_its_criterion(tmp_path, windows, overrides, criterion, expected):
    _, acceptance = cpm.collect(full_batch(tmp_path, windows, **overrides), windows, None, repeats=2)
    problems = acceptance["criteria"][criterion]["problems"]
    assert any(expected in p for p in problems), failed(acceptance)


def test_missing_and_unlisted_protocols_fail_completeness(tmp_path, windows):
    batch = full_batch(tmp_path, windows)
    write_positions(batch, [(p, c, s) for p, (c, s) in enumerate(zip(cpm.ORDER, STAMPS), start=1) if p < 6])
    problems = cpm.collect(batch, windows, None, repeats=2)[1]["criteria"]["5 completeness"]["problems"]
    assert any("position 6 (A) has no protocol" in p for p in problems)
    assert any(f"protocol {STAMPS[5]} is not in positions.tsv" in p for p in problems)


def test_changed_inputs_fail_criterion_2(tmp_path, windows):
    batch = full_batch(tmp_path, windows)
    (windows / "windows.parquet").write_bytes(b"changed")
    problems = cpm.collect(batch, windows, None, repeats=2)[1]["criteria"]["2 inputs"]["problems"]
    assert any("changed after the session" in p for p in problems)


def test_check_protocol_reports_runs_without_plans(tmp_path, windows):
    batch = full_batch(tmp_path, windows)
    protocol = next((batch / "A").rglob(f"protocol-{STAMPS[0]}.json"))
    assert cpm.check_protocol_plans(protocol) == []
    (protocol.parent / f"run-{STAMPS[0]}-2" / "plans.json").unlink()
    assert cpm.check_protocol_plans(protocol) == [f"run-{STAMPS[0]}-2: plans.json missing"]
    assert cpm.main(["--check-protocol", str(protocol)]) == 1

input.content:
# Shuffle-partition experiment session helpers (docs/partition-experiment.md, sections 2-3).
# Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) on 2026-10-19 for the author's measurement session.
# Load once in each Terminal window:   source <repository>/docs/partition-session.zsh
# Loading only defines the functions below, sets the variables and changes into the repository;
# nothing runs until a function is called. Type  steps  for the checklist.
#
# Variables, read when the file is loaded (set them before loading to change them):
#   BATCH          batch folder under data/outputs-partitions (default batch-1). A batch is one
#                  A-B-C-C-B-A sequence under one code state; any change to src/, pyproject.toml
#                  or uv.lock needs a new batch (3.4).
#   PART_LOAD_MAX  upper limit for the 5-minute load average before a protocol (default 4.0)
#   PART_BOOT_MIN  minutes since boot before a protocol may start (default 30)
#   PART_WINDOWS, PART_ROOT, PART_REPEATS: only for a dry run on other data (default: the
#                  stride-7 set, data/outputs-partitions, 4 runs per protocol).

REPO=${${(%):-%x}:A:h:h}
cd $REPO || return 1
BATCH=${BATCH:-batch-1}
PART_WINDOWS=${PART_WINDOWS:-data/windows-experiments/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7}
PART_ROOT=${PART_ROOT:-data/outputs-partitions}
PART_REPEATS=${PART_REPEATS:-4}
PART_LOAD_MAX=${PART_LOAD_MAX:-4.0}
PART_BOOT_MIN=${PART_BOOT_MIN:-30}
BATCH_DIR=$PART_ROOT/$BATCH
LOG=$BATCH_DIR/run-log.txt
POSITIONS=$BATCH_DIR/positions.tsv
PART_ORDER=(A B C C B A)
typeset -A PART_FLAGS
PART_FLAGS=(
  A "--shuffle-partitions 200 --coalesce on"
  B "--shuffle-partitions 200 --coalesce off"
  C "--shuffle-partitions 8 --coalesce off"
)
mkdir -p $BATCH_DIR

steps() {
  cat <<EOF
Shuffle-partition session (docs/partition-experiment.md 2-3), batch: $BATCH_DIR
Positions 1-6 are configurations A B C C B A, one protocol each ($PART_REPEATS runs).
Window 1 runs the commands; window 2 runs the watcher. Load this file in each window first.
Never press Ctrl-C in window 1 or close it while a protocol runs (Ctrl-C during pause5 is fine).
Never paste a command that contains a # comment: this zsh does not ignore comments.

For each position n = 1 to 6, in order:
  1. Window 1:  prechecks 'position n'
     want: lowpowermode 0 | 'AC Power' | docker backend: none | java/etf_risk: none |
           apps: only "Terminal" "Finder" | changed code files: 0 | spark scratch folders: 0
     If anything differs, fix it (quit the apps) and run prechecks again.
  2. Window 2:  watch_runs
  3. Window 1:  pause5 && ready && position n
     ready wants: at least 3.0 GiB available, 5-minute load at most $PART_LOAD_MAX,
     booted at least $PART_BOOT_MIN minutes ago. If it fails, nothing starts: wait, then step 3 again.
  4. Window 1 shows measure's summary ("runs started $PART_REPEATS of $PART_REPEATS", every run "ok",
     no "stopped:" line) and "plans: ok in $PART_REPEATS of $PART_REPEATS runs". Record it:
     note 'position n: 4 ok, nothing unusual'        (single quotes; describe anything unusual)
  where   lists the positions run so far.

Abort a run that takes longer than 3x its configuration's predicted median (section 11):
  Window 2: Ctrl-C (stops only the watcher), then  abort_run  and answer y.
  After window 1 prints measure's summary:  after_abort    want: java: none | spark scratch folders: 0

Any stop (a run not ok, measure stopped early, a plans check failed, an abort, position prints STOP):
  stop the session and come back to Claude. Section 3.4 allows one re-run per position in the
  same session; otherwise the batch ends. A change to src/, pyproject.toml or uv.lock ends the
  batch: the next one is loaded with  BATCH=batch-2 source docs/partition-session.zsh
Back to Claude: in window 1,  claude --continue. No git commits during the session.
Run log: $LOG
Positions: $POSITIONS
EOF
}

_scratch_count() {
  find "$TMPDIR" /private/tmp -maxdepth 1 \( -name 'spark-*' -o -name 'blockmgr-*' \) 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

_boot_minutes() {
  local boot
  boot=$(sysctl -n kern.boottime | sed -E 's/^\{ sec = ([0-9]+),.*/\1/')
  echo $(( ($(date +%s) - boot) / 60 ))
}

prechecks() {
  {
    echo "=== ${1:-protocol}: checks at $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ), batch $BATCH"
    pmset -g | grep lowpowermode
    pmset -g batt | head -n 1
    pgrep -fl com.docker.backend || echo "docker backend: none"
    pgrep -fl 'java|etf_risk' || echo "java/etf_risk: none"
    echo "apps: $(lsappinfo visibleProcessList | grep -o '"[^"]*"' | tr '\n' ' ')"
    echo "load average: $(sysctl -n vm.loadavg)"
    echo "minutes since boot: $(_boot_minutes)"
    echo "HEAD $(git -C $REPO rev-parse --short HEAD), changed code files: $(git -C $REPO status --porcelain -- src pyproject.toml uv.lock | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    echo "spark scratch folders: $(_scratch_count)"
  } | tee -a $LOG
}

pause5() {
  echo "pause start $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)" | tee -a $LOG
  caffeinate -i sleep 300 || { echo "pause interrupted $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)" | tee -a $LOG; return 1; }
  echo "pause end $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)" | tee -a $LOG
}

# The 3.2 readings just before a start; fails, and nothing starts, unless all three are met.
ready() {
  local min=${1:-3.0} gib load5 boot problems=0
  gib=$(uv run --group measure python -c "import psutil; print(round(psutil.virtual_memory().available / 2**30, 2))") || return 2
  load5=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $3}')
  boot=$(_boot_minutes)
  echo "available GiB: $gib (minimum $min); 5-minute load: $load5 (limit $PART_LOAD_MAX); minutes since boot: $boot (minimum $PART_BOOT_MIN)" | tee -a $LOG
  (( gib >= min )) || { echo "  below $min GiB" | tee -a $LOG; problems=1; }
  (( load5 <= PART_LOAD_MAX )) || { echo "  load above $PART_LOAD_MAX" | tee -a $LOG; problems=1; }
  (( boot >= PART_BOOT_MIN )) || { echo "  booted less than $PART_BOOT_MIN minutes ago" | tee -a $LOG; problems=1; }
  (( problems == 0 )) && return 0
  echo "protocol not started" | tee -a $LOG
  return 1
}

# One protocol at position n (2.4): the configuration comes from the order, the protocol JSON from
# what measure wrote. Then the plans check (3.3) and one line in positions.tsv (3.4).
position() {
  local n=$1 config out before proto rc check result
  [[ $n == <1-6> ]] || { echo "usage: position 1-6"; return 2; }
  [[ $PWD == $REPO ]] || { echo "run from $REPO"; return 2; }
  config=${PART_ORDER[$n]}
  out=$BATCH_DIR/$config
  before=$(find $out -name 'protocol-*.json' 2>/dev/null | sort)
  echo "=== position $n (configuration $config): measure starts $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" | tee -a $LOG
  caffeinate -i uv run --group measure python -m etf_risk.measure --repeats $PART_REPEATS -- \
    --windows $PART_WINDOWS --out-root $out ${=PART_FLAGS[$config]} --record-plans 2>&1 | tee -a $LOG
  rc=${pipestatus[1]}
  proto=$(comm -13 <(print -r -- "$before") <(find $out -name 'protocol-*.json' 2>/dev/null | sort) | tail -n 1)
  if [[ -z $proto ]]; then
    echo "STOP: position $n wrote no protocol JSON (measure exit $rc); come back to Claude" | tee -a $LOG
    return 1
  fi
  uv run python analysis/collect_partition_measurements.py --check-protocol $proto | tee -a $LOG
  check=${pipestatus[1]}
  (( check == 0 )) && result=ok || result=failed
  [[ -f $POSITIONS ]] || print -r -- $'position\tconfig\tprotocol\tmeasure_exit\tplans_check\tlogged_at_utc' > $POSITIONS
  print -r -- "$n"$'\t'"$config"$'\t'"${${proto:t:r}#protocol-}"$'\t'"$rc"$'\t'"$result"$'\t'"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> $POSITIONS
  echo "position $n ($config): ${proto:t}, measure exit $rc, plans check $result" | tee -a $LOG
  (( rc == 0 && check == 0 )) || { echo "STOP: a run did not end ok or lacks its plans; come back to Claude" | tee -a $LOG; return 1; }
}

where() {
  if [[ -f $POSITIONS ]]; then column -t -s $'\t' $POSITIONS; else echo "no protocol yet in $BATCH_DIR"; fi
}

watch_runs() {
  local pid
  until pgrep -qf etf_risk.measure; do sleep 5; done
  while pgrep -qf etf_risk.measure; do
    pid=$(pgrep -f etf_risk.spark_pipeline | head -n 1)
    [[ -n $pid ]] && echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S)  pipeline $pid  running $(ps -o etime= -p $pid | tr -d ' ')"
    sleep 10
  done
  echo "measure finished"
}

# 3.3: kill the pipeline process only, never measure, so the protocol JSON is still written.
abort_run() {
  local pid age
  pid=$(pgrep -f etf_risk.spark_pipeline | head -n 1)
  [[ -n $pid ]] || { echo "no pipeline running"; return 1; }
  age=$(ps -o etime= -p $pid | tr -d ' ')
  ps -o pid=,etime=,command= -p $pid
  read -q "?Kill this pipeline process (measure keeps running and records it)? [y/n] " || { echo; return 1; }
  echo
  kill $pid && echo "$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) aborted: killed pipeline $pid after $age" | tee -a $LOG
}

after_abort() {
  {
    echo "=== after abort $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    pgrep -fl java || echo "java: none"
    echo "spark scratch folders: $(_scratch_count)"
  } | tee -a $LOG
}

note() {
  echo "$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) $*" | tee -a $LOG
}

echo "partition-session loaded: batch $BATCH_DIR, run log $LOG; type  steps  for the checklist"
